long_biography.plain_text:
After earning a business-administration degree from Boston University, Luis Miguel Castillo joined Guatemala’s long-established family bottler in 1995. He learned the business through managerial and board roles, then redirected it from a domestic soft-drink operation toward regional scale. As chairman, he used partnerships, acquisitions and brand development to push the company beyond its home market.

Under Castillo, Grupo Mariposa combined CBC’s bottling and distribution network with Beliv’s functional drinks and Bia Foods’ coffee, culinary products and snacks. The group reached Latin American and United States markets, while its capital-markets programme included an international sustainability-linked bond. Castillo also promoted meritocratic management and educational initiatives through Guatefuturo. He died unexpectedly in 2023, days after receiving the BRAVO Visionary Business Leader award.

uncertainties.detail: The authoritative input incorrectly records Castillo as Alive. Grupo Mariposa's exact-name memorial and multiple independent sources establish his death on 25 October 2023 at age 50. Mortality is proposed for correction; dependent death fields remain review candidates because inventory classifies them as inapplicable until that correction is accepted.

Official company and independent business sources establish birth year 1973 and Guatemala as the birth country, which is already stored. No strong source reviewed supplies a complete birth day and month or a city of birth, so those fields remain unproposed.

The four-generation Castillo family beverage enterprise and Castillo's later directorship are well documented, as is his material transformation of the company. The precise probate, trust or inter vivos mechanism by which he received his family-company interest is not public, so Inherited and expanded is scored below maximum confidence.

Bia Foods calls Castillo a co-founder of that later food platform, but Grupo Mariposa and CBC predated him by generations and were the core family enterprise. Operator therefore better describes his principal relationship to the overall wealth-producing assets than Founder or passive family shareholder.

Forbes México published both a historical company article and a sponsored memorial and maintains a tag page for Luis Miguel Castillo. None is a dedicated personal Forbes profile, so no Forbes social is proposed.

No identity-verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok, Wikipedia page or personal website met the verification threshold. The official CBC company website is proposed because it publishes his exact-name memorial and documents the core enterprise.

Public Guatefuturo audit records identify Castillo as board president and contain institutional findings, but reviewed material does not attribute misconduct to him personally. Routine audit detail is excluded from the biography and no adverse personal claim is made.
